reason: The hypothesis synthesizes two separate bodies of literature—the temperature-driven screw-to-edge dislocation transition (from P5, P13, P16, P17, P42, P47) and the influence of short-range order on plasticity (from P14, P26, P27, P28, P30, P31, P32)—and links them through a new mechanistic proposal: that thermally induced SRO mediates the dislocation mode transition, which in turn explains the coupled elastic anisotropy and thermal expansion responses in HfNbTaTiZr. No single passage proposes this integrated mechanism, and the specific prediction that controlled SRO will modulate the yield plateau, elastic modulus retention, and thermal expansion goes beyond the existing evidence.
